name: Mont-Saint-Michel, Normandy
note: The tidal island of Mont-Saint-Michel in its bay, on the border of Normandy and Brittany: the granite rock (about 80 m) crowned by the Benedictine abbey (abbey church with its Romanesque nave and Flamboyant Gothic choir, the Merveille on the north face, the neo-Gothic spire of 1897 with Fremiet's gilded Saint Michael at about 157 m above the sands), the walled village climbing the Grande Rue on the south-east, the ramparts and towers of the Hundred Years' War, and the 2014 passerelle footbridge (Dietmar Feichtinger) crossing the sands to the south. Scale 1.4 blocks per metre; 4480 blocks a side (half 1600 m), centred 970 m south of the rock: the bay's sands round the Mont, the whole passerelle and the causeway-dike, the Couesnon dam, and the mainland at La Caserne (hotels, car parks, polders).
